title: Topology-aware kernel bundle generator and onboarding workflow for MoE/GQA/MHA families
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We onboard an increasing variety of attention-family models (MoE, GQA, MHA) with divergent sharding/topology and sequence-length profiles. Existing compile flows produce monolithic kernel artifacts that either overfit one topology or require manual retuning per model leading to brittle rollouts and frequent rollbacks. This ticket delivers an automated generator that emits compact, topology-aware kernel bundles and a controlled publishing/onboarding workflow to pin appropriate kernel variants per model fingerprint and hardware class.

Scope:
- Build a kernel-bundle generator that takes model fingerprint (num_heads, head_dim, hidden_size, expert_count, expert_shard_map, gqa_grouping, typical_seq_len_distribution) and outputs 2-4 prioritized kernel variants (fast, memory-saver, expert-sharded, fallback).
- Integrate bundle metadata with the profile registry: semantic bundle versioning (bundle_v{major}.{minor}.{patch}), hardware_compat list, seq_len_target buckets, and compatibility flags.
- Add autosuggest rules in the model-onboarder UI/CLI to recommend initial pin (e.g., bundle_v1.0 -> a100-40gb,a100-80gb; bundle_v1.1 -> ampere_xl-32gb) based on telemetry fingerprinting.
- Implement compile-time flags and runtime handshake adapter for MoE routing so that expert-sharded kernels are loaded only when the model+shard layout matches.
- Publish metric dashboards to validate latency/throughput/mem for each bundle and wire up rollout canaries with automatic rollback triggers.

Non-goals: full JIT recompile service on-demand; training-time optimizations; support for every exotic sharding strategy in first iteration.
acceptance_criteria: Kernel-bundle generator accepts model fingerprints and emits 2-4 variants with manifest metadata
Each bundle published to profile registry with semver-like name and hardware_compat list
Model-onboarder suggests a pin for new model uploads in >90% of sampled cases based on historical telemetry mapping
Canary rollout workflow executes 1% -> 10% -> 100% traffic steps with automated rollback if P95 latency regresses >20% or error rate increases >2x
Telemetry dashboard shows per-bundle P50/P95 latency, GPU memory usage, KV cache hit rate and throughput for at least three representative models (one MHA, one GQA, one MoE)
Documentation pages for bundle format, pin policy, and operator rollback steps published to Confluence

perf_bench_summary: Representative microbenchmarks against a100-80gb and ampere_xl-32gb. For 'falcon-like-mha-4b': bundle_v1.0 P50 latency -3.8% (seq_len=512), P95 stable within 2%. Memory -12%. For 'gqa-8g-7b' (gqa_grouping=8): bundle_v1.1 P50 -6.2% (seq_len=256), P95 -1.5%. For 'moe-32e-7b' expert-sharded kernel: throughput +18% with expert-sharded variant vs fallback; P95 improved 9% but memory growth +6%. Full harness results attached in artifacts link.
rollback_plan: Immediate rollback triggers: if P95 latency regresses >20% vs baseline or request error rate increases >2x during canary, automatically pin back to previous bundle (bundle_vX.Y) and drain canary. Manual steps: 1) pause propagation in profile registry, 2) rollback pin using model-onboarder CLI, 3) mark incident and open follow-up ENG ticket for root cause. Playbook in Confluence link above.
rollout_plan: Step 1: Internal dev canary - deploy bundles to dedicated-dev cluster and run synthetic traffic (0% external) for 48h
Step 2: 1% production traffic canary for 24h with full telemetry collection
Step 3: 10% production traffic for 24h, automated gating checks; if green -> 100%
Step 4: Promote bundle to 'stable' in profile registry and tag release
notes: Design feedback (DES-442): Add visual indicator in Console showing active bundle and fallback behavior
PM note: tie the onboard suggestion to cost estimator so customers see estimated unit cost delta
Engineering trade-off: producing 4 variants increases storage/registry complexity but reduces rollout risk by offering memory/latency trade-offs
